clue.text: Period of time without energy? Heading for detox unit

indicators.note: without means the energy letter is left out of the period of time

parts.note: a year is a period of time
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so this takes the start of detox

explanation.surface: A query about time spent off energy, then a nod to a rehab clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for detox' looks like a phrase about rehab; it is just the first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a unit of length, three feet in the imperial system.

clue.text: Tackle illegal drugs equipment 1 9 used?

definitions.meaning: fishing or sporting kit, as in fishing tackle
Yardbird (1 and 9 together) was Charlie Parker's nickname; the kit a musician uses, with a hint at his drug use

explanation.surface: A police raid seizing narcotics and the paraphernalia a jazzman was hooked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 and 9 read together give YARDBIRD, the nickname of saxophonist Charlie Parker, theme of the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers kit and tackle generally, and is also British slang for illicit narcotics.

clue.text: Raising of part of the earth's crust alters a pH value

definitions.text: Raising of part of the earth's crust

indicators.note: alters tells us the letters of the following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A geology note: a change in acidity reading shifts the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alters' shuffles the letters of A PH VALUE.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an upheaval is an uplift of rock strata, a lifting of the crust.

clue.text: With resentful reluctance, king finally ordered drink in unpleasant setting

parts.note: GR is George Rex, King George

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the unpleasant word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: ugly can mean unpleasant, as in an ugly scene

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word ordered

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A monarch, at last, demands a drink in a seedy bar and is served grumpily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king' gives GR (Georgius Rex); 'setting' wraps the unpleasant word round the last letter of 'ordered' and the drink, like a jewel in its mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something grudgingly means doing it unwillingly and with resentment.

clue.text: Essential feature of theme's called for an intoxicant

indicators.note: the essential feature lies inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something central to a theme gets named as the cause of intoxication.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescal is a Mexican distilled spirit, a strong alcoholic drink, so it intoxicates.

clue.text: Daily pork pie? Fool!

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady in British usage
pork pie is rhyming slang for lie (pork pie = lie)

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a newspaper's tall story and calls the writer a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; it is a daily cleaner, a char. 'Pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a silly person, as in 'a right charlie'.

clue.text: Difficult time crossing river in Scotland inspired saxophonist originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its opening letter, across the six words before it

explanation.surface: A musician's rough patch, a journey over a Scottish river, gives him inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' applies to all six words before it, not just to 'saxophonist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of intense trouble or danger, a turning point.

clue.text: As it happens, rear part of bar is what gets damaged after too much drink is taken

definitions.text: what gets damaged after too much drink is taken

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

indicators.note: the rear part of a word is its last letter, taken from bar

explanation.surface: A live report from the back of a pub on what heavy drinking ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy alcohol use harms this organ, causing cirrhosis.

clue.text: Butler and chauffeur for American writer

definitions.meaning: Lady Penelope's manservant who also drives her pink Rolls-Royce in the puppet series Thunderbirds
Dorothy ..., the American wit and poet

explanation.surface: A household servant who also drives being recast as a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Also the surname of Charlie 'Bird' Parker, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname fits both Thunderbirds' manservant and the New York humorist Dorothy.

clue.text: Offer around right time

indicators.note: around means the offer word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: A bidder making an offer just at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is prison time: 'doing bird' is British slang for serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time.

clue.text: Get-up-and-go extremely depleted finally? Yes, then doubly so

indicators.note: depleted at its finish means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: very means extremely

indicators.note: doubly so means do the same depleting twice, so two closing letters go

parts.note: the yes repeats the step: take the same word for extremely again

explanation.surface: Energy so drained it is nearly gone, and then drained twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: VERY less its last letter is VER; 'Yes, then doubly so' repeats with two letters gone, VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is energy and enthusiasm, the same thing as drive or get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Type of 9 to avoid

definitions.meaning: 9 is a bird; a mallard is one sort of this waterfowl
to dodge, as in ... a question

explanation.surface: A kind of bird to keep away from.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a water bird and also means to dodge or evade.

clue.text: 9 with two articles stolen from feather hat

parts.note: 9 is a bird, here a tit

indicators.note: stolen from means those letters are taken out of feather

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A bird robbed of two items from its plumes, recast as millinery.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is Cockney rhyming slang: tit-for-tat = hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Titfer is British rhyming slang for a hat, from tit-for-tat.

clue.text: Premier beat Trump's story

parts.note: premier means first
to floor someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A prime minister trounces the American president in a news tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' is the storey of a building; to an American like Trump the first floor is street level.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor of a building is a storey; Trump Tower has one at ground level by US counting.

clue.text: Seduce bandmate ultimately, by wild living (with injected drug)

indicators.note: injected means the drug letter is put into the rearranged letters
wild means the letters of living are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of bandmate

explanation.surface: A rock musician's wild, drug-fuelled lifestyle used to lure a fellow band member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges LIVING to INVIGL, 'injected' puts E inside it, and E from 'bandmate ultimately' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or entice by flattery, much like to lure or tempt.

clue.text: German setter with yellow fluid in veins, as myth has it

definitions.text: fluid in veins, as myth has it

parts.note: the setter says 'I', which in German is ich
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A German dog with golden fluid flowing in its veins, the stuff of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German setter' looks like a dog breed; it is the setter (I) in German.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the gods' veins instead of blood.

clue.text: Study of 9s involved only two 11s? Right!

indicators.note: involved means mixed up, so these letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: 11 is duck, and a duck is a zero score in cricket, so two of them are OO

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's tally of only two ducks gets a sarcastic 'Right!'
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is zero in cricket, a batsman out without scoring, giving the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithology is the scientific study of birds, and 9 stands for bird here.

clue.text: Invigorating no-go area, in parts even attractive

indicators.note: no means the following letters are absent from invigorating

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the even parts of area, its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A bracing place you cannot enter, partly appealing nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes GO and RA (the even letters of 'area', from 'in parts even') from INVIGORATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inviting is tempting and appealing, drawing one in.

clue.text: In concert, playing duet with flipping hot content

indicators.note: content means the turned word is held within the rearranged letters
playing means the letters of duet are performed in a new order
flipping turns the fashionable word end to end

parts.note: in, as in fashionable, means hot

explanation.surface: Two musicians performing a duet with a fiery passion at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is IN in the sense of fashionable, not heat; 'playing' and 'flipping' both act before 'content' places one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act together, joined as one.

clue.text: Never mind wife always clutching 12

indicators.note: clutching means the two letters groups hold the hat in their grasp

parts.note: ever means always
12 is titfer, a hat

explanation.surface: A shrug as a spouse forever hangs on to her favourite headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever, said dismissively, means it does not matter, much like forget it.

clue.text: Piece from the i: "Fertility's a little lower"

definitions.note: lower here means one that lows, a cow

indicators.note: a piece is a part, so the letters are lifted from inside these words

explanation.surface: An extract from the i newspaper on fertility being slightly down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'less high' but 'something that lows', a cow; a little cow is a young one. The i is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not calved, so a small mooing beast.

clue.text: Outside the range of female singer, with two final notes replaced by one in between

indicators.text: with two final notes replaced by one in between
indicators.note: her name ends in two notes of the scale, which give way to the single note lying between them

parts.note: Beyoncé is a female pop singer

explanation.surface: A diva hits notes too high for her range and has to swap them.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters C and E are musical notes; the note between them is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond means further than or past, so outside the range of something.

clue.text: Vacuously bizarre dance music, jazz style

indicators.note: vacuously means emptied, so only the outside letters of bizarre stay

parts.note: bop is dance music, or to dance to pop

explanation.surface: A sneer at weird, empty dance tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is the fast, complex jazz style Charlie Parker pioneered in the 1940s.

clue.text: Lad is drunk after Savoy's first quit for another label (the mug!)

indicators.note: drunk means the remaining letters reel into a new order
quit means that letter leaves the words before it
first takes the opening letter of Savoy's

explanation.surface: A tipsy lad leaves the Savoy and gets called a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for another label' says the answer is another name for the mug; the Savoy is a grand London hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial is British slang for the face, just as mug is.

clue.text: Beat time unevenly, her combo following

indicators.note: following means those letters come after the time letter
unevenly takes the odd-numbered letters of the words her and combo

explanation.surface: A drummer with a ragged rhythm, her group trailing along.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: A 6's taken after two artists, becoming an unusually exceptional 9

indicators.note: taken after means the A and six come behind the artists

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist; two give RARA
VI is six in Roman numerals, plus S from the 's

explanation.surface: A troubled painter's tale becomes a story of an extraordinary bird.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' is not a cross-reference here but the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'rare bird', used for a remarkably unusual person or thing.

clue.text: Type of sax is key, by end of solo

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of solo

explanation.surface: A saxophone's key and a solo's closing passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The alto saxophone is a mid-range member of the saxophone family, Parker's instrument.

clue.text: See 23
Horse 1 9's straddling

indicators.note: straddling means the bird sits astride the one

parts.note: 9 is bird, so a type of bird, a heron
1 is I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jockey and a bird mounted on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is street slang for the drug; 1 is the Roman I, not the cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is drug slang for heroin, the narcotic Charlie Parker was addicted to.

clue.text: Backing for each song that's made a comeback

indicators.note: backing means the word for each is turned to face the other way

parts.note: per means for each
a Lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: A backing track for every song in a musician's comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Replied means answered, a retort or comeback in words.
